candidates.statement: D. Regulatory Requirements for Testing to Reduce the Risk of TTM 160 Malaria is a relevant transfusion-transmitted infection (RTTI) (21 CFR 630.3(h)(1)(x)). 161 Under 21 CFR 610.40(a)(3)(i), blood establishments must test for certain RTTI, including 162 malaria, when 1) a test is licensed, approved or cleared by FDA for use as a donor 163 screening test and is available for such use; and 2) testing is necessary to reduce 164 adequately and appropriately the risk of transmission of the RTTI by blood, or blood 165 component, or blood derivative product manufactured from the collected blood or blood 166 component. The regulations require blood establishments to perform this testing on 167 every donation unless an exception applies. Under 21 CFR 610.40(a)(3)(ii), when 168 evidence related to the risk of transmission of the RTTI supports that testing of each 169 donation is not necessary to reduce adequately and appropriately the risk of transmission 170 of such infection by blood, blood component, or blood derivative product manufactured 171 from the collected blood or blood component, blood establishments may adopt an 172 adequate and appropriate alternative testing procedure that has been found acceptable for 173 this purpose by FDA (21 CFR 610.40(a)(3)(ii)(A)) or stop testing in accordance with 174 procedures found acceptable for this purpose by FDA (21 CFR 610.40(a)(3)(ii)(B)). 175
candidates.context: Another disadvantage of the current donor screening measures for malaria is the deferral 147 of large numbers of otherwise healthy individuals based on travel risk and prior residence 148 in malaria-endemic countries. According to some estimates, about 1% of all individuals 149 who present to donate blood report malaria risk factors, amounting to an estimated 150 150,000 donations that are deferred for this reason (Ref. 13). Moreover, the deferral of 151 travelers and prior residents of malaria-endemic countries in Africa, Asia and South 152 America limits the genetic diversity of the blood supply. Having a predominantly 153 Caucasian donor base with other ethnic groups underrepresented in the U.S. blood supply 154 makes it difficult to find compatible blood for some patients. For example, rare or 155 matched blood types needed by transfusion-dependent patients with diseases such as 156

candidates.statement: Malaria-endemic country - Any country having an area or areas with malaria where CDC 408 recommends anti-malarial chemoprophylaxis for travelers in the CDC Yellow Book: Health 409 Information for International Travel commonly known as ( The Yellow Book ) at the time the 410 donor is screened. A country that has any malaria-endemic areas should be considered to be 411 malaria-endemic in its entirety. 412
candidates.context: History of Malaria - Malaria is an infectious disease caused by a parasitic protozoan of the 401 genus Plasmodium . A malaria diagnosis or a history of malaria in a prospective donor is based 402 on a positive diagnostic test indicating Plasmodium infection, or a determination of a history of 403 malaria made by the blood establishment’s responsible physician. A prospective donor who had 404 a reactive donor screening test for Plasmodia spp . nucleic acid is also considered to have a 405 history of malaria. 406 Residence in a malaria-endemic country - For purposes of this guidance, residence is defined 414 as a continuous stay of 5 years or more in a malaria-endemic country or countries. 415
